ridings.name: North Vancouver-Lonsdale
ridings.communities: Lower Lonsdale, Central Lonsdale, Norgate, and the urban core of the City of North Vancouver.
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: None found. Bowinn Ma has been NDP MLA since 2017; Wikipedia lists her as Minister of Infrastructure (earlier Emergency Management).

candidates.name: Joshua A Singer Johnson
candidates.bio: Lawyer and lifelong North Vancouver resident with experience in constitutional and Indigenous litigation, human rights and tenant advocacy; law degree from McGill.

candidates.name: Bowinn Ma
candidates.bio: Engineer and project manager at Vancouver airport before politics; MLA since 2017. Wikipedia lists her as Minister of Infrastructure, after serving as Minister of Emergency Management.

candidates.name: Trevor Withers
candidates.bio: Data visualization engineer at Aritzia and Queen's University graduate; has worked at a North Vancouver pub, played junior hockey with the Wolfpack and refereed minor hockey.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

ridings.notes: Ballot list from Elections BC. 2024 had only two candidates (no Green).

ridings.name: North Vancouver-Seymour
ridings.communities: Most of the District of North Vancouver: Upper Lonsdale, Carisbrooke, Upper Delbrook, Lynn Valley, Capilano University area, Tsleil-Waututh Nation, and east of the Seymour River to Deep Cove.
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: None found. Susie Chant is a Parliamentary Secretary (Seniors' Services and Long-Term Care) per Wikipedia. Conservative Lynne Block, the sitting West Vancouver-Capilano MLA, was moved here to run against her.

candidates.name: Lynne Block
candidates.bio: Educator and former West Vancouver school trustee; elected Conservative MLA for West Vancouver-Capilano in 2024 and now running in North Vancouver-Seymour instead.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

candidates.name: Susie Chant
candidates.bio: Registered nurse and long-serving Royal Canadian Navy Reserve member; NDP MLA since 2020 and Parliamentary Secretary for Seniors' Services and Long-Term Care.

candidates.name: Lori Climenhaga
candidates.bio: Deep Cove resident for over 16 years; former director with the BC government and the BC Chamber of Commerce, with 25 years in government, business and community work.

candidates.name: Ben Holt
candidates.bio: Software team lead and systems administrator raised in North Vancouver-Seymour; chaired the Mount Fromme Residents Association and coaches youth soccer and baseball.

candidates.name: Frederick Thiele
candidates.bio: Born and raised in North Vancouver; local business owner with over 25 years in technology, per the preview of his VoteMate profile..

ridings.notes: Communities from a North Shore News 2024 riding brief seen via search summary (secondary). 2024 independent was Mitchell Baker.

ridings.name: Vancouver-Fraserview
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: Incumbent George Chow (NDP, former Minister of Citizens' Services) is not seeking re-election (announced Sept 27, 2026, per Wikipedia). Aman Singh replaced him as NDP candidate.

candidates.name: Francoise Raunet
candidates.bio: Public school teacher and vice president of the Vancouver Elementary and Adult Educators Society, on leave from the classroom; ran for BC Greens in Point Grey in 2011 and 2013.

candidates.name: Deep Sandhu
candidates.bio: Businessman and longshoreman with experience in forestry, real estate and asset management; Vancouver resident for over 35 years and former Canadian Armed Forces reservist.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

candidates.name: Aman Singh
candidates.bio: Lawyer; NDP MLA for Richmond-Queensborough 2020 to 2024, lost that seat in 2024; BC NDP president since November 2025.

ridings.notes: No sitting MLA is on the ballot.

ridings.name: Vancouver-Hastings
ridings.communities: Hastings-Sunrise and half of Grandview-Woodland (per a BIV 2024 riding brief seen via search summary; boundaries unchanged for 2024).
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: None found. Niki Sharma is Deputy Premier and Attorney General per Wikipedia.

candidates.name: Christian Bosio
candidates.bio: Mechanical engineer and clean hydrogen entrepreneur who co-founded a company with over 300 employees; Commercial Drive resident for 12 years and youth soccer volunteer coach.

candidates.name: Kimball Cariou
candidates.bio: Longtime Communist candidate and BC party leader from December 2020 to 2025; ran in Vancouver-Strathcona in 2024 and Vancouver-Hastings in 2017 and 2020.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Communist Party of British Columbia

candidates.name: Kyra Philbert
candidates.bio: Registered nurse with over a decade in healthcare; holds a UBC nursing master's degree and a bachelor's in gender, race, sexuality and social justice.

candidates.name: Niki Sharma
candidates.bio: Lawyer and former Stand.earth campaigner; Vancouver-Hastings MLA, now Deputy Premier and Attorney General.

candidates.name: Phyllis Tang
candidates.bio: Piano teacher for 25 years and community outreach worker; former constituency assistant to a Richmond-Queensborough MLA; ran for Vancouver city council in 2018.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

candidates.name: Phil Webb
candidates.bio: No biography found. Elections BC lists him as the Libertarian candidate; BC Ballot shows no earlier run on record.

ridings.name: Vancouver-Kensington
ridings.communities: Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Sunset, and parts of Renfrew-Collingwood along the Kingsway corridor (from search summary; Wikipedia gives no list).
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: None found. Mable Elmore was a parliamentary secretary until November 2024; no current cabinet role per Wikipedia.

candidates.name: Mable Elmore
candidates.bio: Former Coast Mountain bus driver; NDP MLA for Vancouver-Kensington since 2009 and parliamentary secretary until November 2024.

candidates.name: Adam Hawk
candidates.bio: Organic foods industry professional and Vancouver resident since 2006; past board member of the Vancouver Greens; ran for BC Greens in Vancouver-South Granville in 2024.

candidates.name: Aron Lageri
candidates.bio: Medical imaging technologist turned health-care manager with 22 years of experience, including False Creek Surgical Centre; ran for the Conservatives in Vancouver-South Granville in 2024.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

ridings.name: Vancouver-Langara
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: None found. Sunita Dhir is Parliamentary Secretary for International Credentials per Wikipedia.

candidates.name: John Atoyebi
candidates.bio: Lawyer and former magistrate and district court judge in Nigeria; former investigator with the BC Ombudsperson; sits on a City of Vancouver disability advisory committee.

candidates.name: Alan Beesley
candidates.bio: Lawyer called to the BC bar in 1989; ran a Tofino business including a restaurant and fish buying station from 2000 to 2019; son of a Canadian diplomat.

candidates.name: Sunita Dhir
candidates.bio: Former S.U.C.C.E.S.S. language instructor; NDP MLA for Vancouver-Langara and Parliamentary Secretary for International Credentials.

candidates.name: Jaime Stein
candidates.bio: Business and non-profit executive and former broadcast journalist; born and raised in Vancouver and a graduate of Point Grey Secondary.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

ridings.name: Vancouver-Little Mountain
ridings.communities: Riley Park, South Cambie, parts of Mount Pleasant and part of Oakridge (from search summary; Wikipedia gives no list). New riding in 2024.
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: None found. Christine Boyle is Minister of Housing and Municipal Affairs since July 2025 (earlier Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation), per Wikipedia.

candidates.name: Christine Boyle
candidates.bio: Climate activist and ordained United Church minister; Vancouver city councillor 2018 to 2024; MLA since 2024 and Minister of Housing and Municipal Affairs since July 2025.

candidates.name: Sarah MacLeod
candidates.bio: Former film assistant director now in fundraising and advocacy; attended Vancouver City Council meetings for over a year and spoke on tree canopy and supportive housing.

candidates.name: Alex Muir
candidates.bio: UBC political science graduate and Team BC rugby player with a Canada U20 cap; worked as a communications staffer in the Official Opposition leader's office in Ottawa.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

ridings.name: Vancouver-Point Grey
ridings.communities: West Point Grey, western Kitsilano, University Endowment Lands, UBC Point Grey campus.
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: None. David Eby is Premier (since Nov 18, 2022) and NDP leader; he dissolved the legislature on Sept 22, 2026.

candidates.name: Michael Davis
candidates.bio: Recently retired head of a communications and government relations firm; former director of communications to Canada's Justice Minister; founder of OurKidsClimate.ca.

candidates.name: David Eby
candidates.bio: Premier of British Columbia since November 2022; Point Grey MLA since 2013; former Attorney General and housing minister.

candidates.name: Alex McMillan
candidates.bio: Interim CEO of the BC Chamber of Commerce until February; runs a consultancy started in 2020; former provincial political staffer and civil servant.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

candidates.name: Beatrice Sharpe
candidates.bio: University of Victoria student in political science and environmental studies; former chair of the Young BC Greens and chair of Green Nation Collective Changemakers.

ridings.name: Vancouver-Quilchena
ridings.communities: Quilchena, Kerrisdale, Arbutus Ridge, parts of Shaughnessy.
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: Dallas Brodie was elected as a Conservative, removed from the Conservative caucus March 7, 2025, co-founded OneBC June 9, 2025, and sits as OneBC. Wikipedia notes she was removed as OneBC interim leader Dec 13, 2025 and reinstated Dec 21. A 2026 recall bid against her failed.

candidates.name: Carson Binda
candidates.bio: Former BC director of the Canadian Taxpayers Federation (joined 2022); campaign staffer at three levels of government; served as a logistics officer in the army reserves.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

candidates.name: Dallas Brodie
candidates.bio: Lawyer and broadcaster; elected as a Conservative in 2024, removed from caucus in March 2025, co-founded OneBC in June 2025. Sitting MLA for this riding.

candidates.name: Douglas Courtemanche
candidates.bio: Semi-retired craniofacial surgeon and UBC clinical professor since 2008; grew up in Vancouver-Quilchena; former Medical Staff President at BC Children's and Women's Hospital.

candidates.name: Petra Kuret
candidates.bio: Former Accenture managing partner for British Columbia and Vancity senior vice president; sought the federal Liberal nomination in Vancouver Quadra in 2025; Quilchena resident 40 years.

candidates.name: Callista Ryan
candidates.bio: Communications professional, co-chair of the BC Young New Democrats and board director of the BC Council for Families; NDP candidate here in 2024, finishing second.

ridings.notes: 2024 winner Brodie ran as Conservative; she is now OneBC (result_2024.party shows her 2024 party). 2024 shares: Independent Caroline Ying-Mei Wang 1.73 percent, Green Michael Barkusky 7.78 percent.

ridings.name: Vancouver-Renfrew
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: None found. Adrian Dix is Minister of Energy and Climate Solutions per Wikipedia.

candidates.name: Adrian Dix
candidates.bio: Former BC NDP leader and Health Minister, earlier a political aide and commentator; now Minister of Energy and Climate Solutions per Wikipedia.

candidates.name: Rebecca Haber
candidates.bio: Public health professional with over 15 years in pregnancy, child health and immunization programs; East Vancouver resident for 17 years and community garden board member.

candidates.name: Tom Ikonomou
candidates.bio: Realtor since 2008 and former restaurant owner; Army veteran and former volunteer firefighter; treasurer of a Burnaby AHEPA chapter.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

candidates.name: Lisa Prescott
candidates.bio: Engineer with over 20 years in public service, including senior roles at the City of Vancouver and BC Hydro, now a consultant; Renfrew resident since 2003.

ridings.name: Vancouver-South Granville
ridings.communities: South Granville, eastern Kitsilano, western Fairview, Granville Island.
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: Incumbent Brenda Bailey (NDP, former finance minister per Wikipedia) is not seeking re-election (announced Sept 23, 2026). Lara Honrado is the NDP candidate.

candidates.name: Maria J Cruz
candidates.bio: Outreach worker in the Vancouver School Board adult education program; culture and heritage planner with a Master of Museum Studies; South Granville renter for 15 years.

candidates.name: Lara Honrado
candidates.bio: Led community relations for Mayor Gregor Robertson; works with the United Nations on public understanding of AI; board member of the 221A cultural land trust.

candidates.name: Lisa Phillips
candidates.bio: Third-generation Vancouverite, finance and technology professional and business owner with a UBC mathematics degree and eight years of board governance experience.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

candidates.name: Colin Smith
candidates.bio: Owner of a Kitsilano construction management firm with an academic background in law, international relations and sociology; area resident for over 30 years.

candidates.name: Salvatore Vetro
candidates.bio: No 2026 biography found. Ran as an Independent in Vancouver-Kensington in 2020, finishing fourth with 202 votes.

ridings.notes: No sitting MLA is on the ballot.

ridings.name: Vancouver-Strathcona
ridings.communities: Eastern downtown, Strathcona, Downtown Eastside, Gastown, and parts of Mount Pleasant, Grandview-Woodland, Kensington-Cedar Cottage and Chinatown.
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: Seat vacant. NDP MLA Joan Phillip died Aug 28, 2026; the by-election was cancelled when the general election was called (per Wikipedia). Amanda Burrows is the NDP candidate.

candidates.name: Amanda Burrows
candidates.bio: Executive director of First United Church in the Downtown Eastside, working in the neighbourhood over a decade; lost the OneCity mayoral nomination earlier in 2026.

candidates.name: Robert Crooks
candidates.bio: Leader of the Communist Party of BC since July 2025; ran in Victoria-Swan Lake in 2024.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Communist Party of British Columbia

candidates.name: Jordan Zheng McIntosh
candidates.bio: Mineral exploration field worker and geological engineering student, born in Vancouver; has volunteered in politics since middle school.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

candidates.name: Tanya Webking
candidates.bio: Dene and German with roots in the Tlicho Nation; decades of frontline work in housing, healthcare and community support in the Downtown Eastside.

ridings.notes: No sitting MLA is on the ballot. 2024 Communist candidate was Kimball Cariou (336 votes).

ridings.name: Vancouver-West End
ridings.communities: West End, Coal Harbour, Davie Village, Stanley Park.
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: None found. Spencer Chandra Herbert is Minister of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation since July 2025 and deputy speaker since 2020, per Wikipedia.

candidates.name: Spencer Chandra Herbert
candidates.bio: Former arts manager and Vancouver park commissioner; MLA since 2008, deputy speaker since 2020 and Minister of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation since July 2025.

candidates.name: Scott MacDonald
candidates.bio: Recently retired physician who practised addictions-focused primary care in downtown Vancouver from 2004 to 2026; earlier medical director of Casey House Hospice in Toronto.

candidates.name: Dion Weisner
candidates.bio: Senior staffer in the Official Opposition leader's office working on public policy and research; previously worked in sales and marketing at Harbour Air.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

ridings.name: Vancouver-Yaletown
ridings.communities: Yaletown and downtown Vancouver east of Burrard Street.
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: None found. Terry Yung is Minister of State for Community Safety and Integrated Services since November 2024 per Wikipedia.

candidates.name: Sam Chandola
candidates.bio: Tech founder who arrived in Canada in 2012 and started First Fund, a pre-seed investment fund; was the Conservative candidate in North Vancouver-Seymour in 2024.

candidates.name: Margareta Dovgal
candidates.bio: National economic commentator and policy analyst with a career in economic development advocacy; born in and lives in downtown Vancouver.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

candidates.name: Priyan Samarakoone
candidates.bio: Housing lawyer called to the BC bar in 2013; spent seven years with Access Pro Bono BC; Yaletown resident for 16 years.

candidates.name: Terry Yung
candidates.bio: Retired Vancouver police inspector with thirty years of service; Vancouver-Yaletown MLA since 2024 and Minister of State for Community Safety and Integrated Services.

ridings.name: West Vancouver-Capilano
ridings.communities: Most of the District of West Vancouver and the Capilano area of the District of North Vancouver.
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: Sitting MLA Lynne Block (Conservative) is running in North Vancouver-Seymour instead; the Conservatives moved her and named Caroline Elliott here. No sitting MLA is on this ballot.

candidates.name: Honieh Barzegari
candidates.bio: Physician by training with over 20 years in healthcare, life sciences and technology; former Ministerial Advisor to the BC government; sits on the Langara College Board of Governors.

candidates.name: Naomi Chocyk
candidates.bio: No biography found. Elections BC lists her as the OneBC candidate; BC Ballot shows no earlier run on record.

candidates.name: Caroline Elliott
candidates.bio: Public policy think tank senior fellow with an SFU political science PhD; former BC legislature adviser to two ministers; lives in North Vancouver; former Conservative leadership candidate.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

candidates.name: Arwa Shurab
candidates.bio: Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant, leadership coach and founder of HERVOICE; board director of the North Shore Restorative Justice Society; North Shore resident.

ridings.name: West Vancouver-Sea to Sky
ridings.communities: West Vancouver west of Cypress Creek, Bowen Island, Lions Bay, Furry Creek, Britannia Beach, Squamish, Whistler, Pemberton, Mount Currie, D'Arcy, and communities near the north end of Harrison Lake.
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: None. Jeremy Valeriote (Green) was named BC Green interim leader in January 2025 and remains the Green MLA at dissolution (per Wikipedia). First BC Green elected on the mainland.

candidates.name: Ayla Dumais
candidates.bio: Raised in Squamish, member of Prophet River First Nation; policy adviser in the Official Opposition leader's office; formerly in community relations at Woodfibre LNG.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC candidate page

candidates.name: Michelle Livaja
candidates.bio: Bowen Island resident for 26 years; works in the Ministry of Infrastructure minister's office after four years as a constituency assistant; NDP candidate here in 2017.

candidates.name: Jeremy Valeriote
candidates.bio: MLA since 2024 and first BC Green elected on the mainland; environmental consultant and former Gibsons councillor; Green interim leader since January 2025.

candidates.name: Dan Wood
candidates.bio: Housing and real estate professional at a provincial Crown organization; West Vancouver resident since 2023; CentreBC communications chair on its provincial executive.

ridings.notes: Closest 2024 margin in this group is Langara (419 votes), then Sea to Sky (676).
